bib.title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Appendix B. Probability Distributions (pp. 685-693)

question: What are the density, mean, variance, mode, entropy and conjugacy relations of the distributions used in the book?

results.claim: All the listed distributions are members of the exponential family.
results.quote: All of these distributions are members of the exponential family and are widely used
results.note: Von Mises, Student's t and Wishart are listed too; Student's t is not an exponential-family member, so the blanket claim is loose.

results.claim: Beta is conjugate to Bernoulli, with a and b as effective prior counts of x=1 and x=0; mean a/(a+b).
results.quote:
a and b can
be interpreted as the effective prior number of observations of x = 1 and x = 0,

results.claim: Dirichlet is the conjugate prior of the multinomial and generalizes the beta.

results.claim: Gamma is conjugate prior for the precision of a univariate Gaussian; a=1 is the exponential distribution.
results.quote:
The gamma distribution is
the conjugate prior for the precision (inverse variance) of a univariate Gaussian.

results.claim: Gaussian entropy: H[x] = 1/2 ln sigma^2 + 1/2 (1+ln(2 pi)); the Gaussian maximizes entropy for a given variance.
results.quote: The Gaussian is the distribution that maximizes the entropy for a given variance

results.claim: Conditional of a joint Gaussian: mean mu_a|b = mu_a - Lambda_aa^-1 Lambda_ab (x_b - mu_b), covariance Lambda_aa^-1; marginal N(x_a|mu_a, Sigma_aa).
Linear-Gaussian marginal: p(y)=N(y|A mu+b, L^-1 + A Lambda^-1 A^T) and posterior covariance Sigma=(Lambda + A^T L A)^-1.
Student's t is an infinite mixture of Gaussians with the same mean and different variances; nu=1 is Cauchy; nu to infinity gives Gaussian; robust to outliers.
results.quote:
Student’s t-distribution provides a generalization of the Gaussian whose
maximum likelihood parameter values are robust to outliers.

results.claim: Student's t variance is (1/lambda) nu/(nu-2), defined for nu>2; mean defined for nu>1.
Wishart is the conjugate prior for the precision matrix of a multivariate Gaussian; in one dimension it is gamma with a=nu/2, b=1/(2W); needs nu > D-1.
results.quote:
In one dimension, the Wishart
reduces to the gamma distribution

results.claim: Von Mises: p(theta)=exp(m cos(theta-theta0))/(2 pi I0(m)); concentration m analogous to precision; approximately Gaussian for large m.
results.quote:
For large m, the von Mises
distribution is approximately a Gaussian centred on θ0.

problems: Internal slips in the printed appendix: (1) Eq B.29 gamma mode says 'for α ≥ 1' but the parameter is a. (2) Eq B.49 writes N(x|...) where x_a is meant. (3) Multinomial entropy B.58 and Eq B.59 index to M though the variable has K states (B.63 then uses K). (4) The intro says all listed distributions are exponential family, yet Student's t (and the mixtures) are not (reader's observation, not the book's). (5) 'Guiness' misspelled. (6) Dirichlet Eq B.17-B.20 use alpha-hat, whose hat is lost in the text layer.
